subject: S12a re-review 2 done: engine-time + repaint gates (negative proven), StickyInkToolbar (+SectionInk), tall dpr-2 page; CI 43990624727 ink green
body:
S12a re-review 2: all three items are done.

Commits on claude/naadi-shared: 22e02f2, b1812fd, fdcb9e7.

CI run 43990624727 (b1812fd): https://github.com/arrowassassin/naadi/actions/runs/43990624727
- Passed: lint/typecheck/unit/drift/build, integration, e2e webkit (187 ink-spec passes, including dpr2 and the https prod gate), e2e firefox (160).
- e2e chromium failed only in ink-sync.spec:290 and :365 (S12b's spec). The same two fail in the runs before my commits (43989861940 at 18f0ec0, 43987646921 at 1508098), so this round did not cause them.
- Run 43990864028 (fdcb9e7, SectionInk switch) is in progress.

1. Scroll guard that does not cancel out
- The engine has a main-thread probe, startProbe()/stopProbe(). It covers the scroll, rAF frame, resize and settle callbacks; the probe wraps the listener, so a slow onScroll is measured. The e2e gate sums every engine on the page per animation frame and requires p95 < 2 ms.
- renderStats has tilesPainted, repaints (a tile painted again with no content change), slabsRestored and parkSkipped.
- After a first pass (steps of 0.4 viewport, repeated until a pass paints nothing, at most 3), the five rounds must paint 0 tiles and make 0 wasted repaints.
- Negative proof, a separate e2e on the laptop profiles: 12 ms of busy-wait wrapped around the stress engine's onScroll at runtime (no production flag). The probe reads p95 13-16 ms on WebKit and 13-20 ms on Chromium; the test requires >= 2 ms, i.e. the gate fails. It passed on CI webkit-laptop-1440.
- Unchanged pages read: engine p95 0-1 ms (max 2-8 ms), tiles painted after the first pass 0, repaints 0.
- To make "no repaint" hold on a page taller than the keep window, slabs that leave the window park their settled PNGs (blob URLs, at most 48 MB, oldest dropped first). When they return they show those pictures instead of repainting. A content change in range, a theme change or a geometry change drops the parked pictures.
- Bug found and fixed: settling waited for tiles of off-screen slabs that were waiting for canvas memory, which only settling frees. On a page taller than the budget it deadlocked (renderPending stayed true for 90 s). Tiles waiting for memory no longer hold settling back.

2. Layer promotion in the shared component
- StickyInkToolbar (placement top or bottom) in apps/web/src/ink/InkToolbar.tsx gives every mount the will-change-transform layer, with a unit test.
- The lab uses it.
- Contract to seg12b: 20261116T233825. seg12b agreed and handed the spot to me (20261117T003157). I switched SectionInk.tsx in fdcb9e7 and posted 20261117T005034.

3. Taller dpr-2 page
- The webkit-ipad-portrait-dpr2 project scrolls a stress page 12 widths tall (?stress_height=12, 2-16 allowed).
- Rounds paint 0 tiles, and 20-28 slabs come back from parked pictures per run (asserted > 0).
- 8 of 8 local repeat runs passed after the fix; without the repeated first pass, 3 of 4 failed.

Local smoke, the last two runs on the rebased tree with --retries=0 and 2 workers:
- smoke-15: 69 passed, 11 skipped (signed-in gate and sync tests need the auth container).
- smoke-16: 69 passed, 11 skipped.
- perf-15 and perf-16: 7 passed each (dpr2 and laptop: latency, scroll, 12 surfaces, engine-time negative).

Local numbers:

| Profile | Scroll ratio | Engine p95 | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| webkit-laptop-1440 | 0.94 | 0 ms | |
| webkit-ipad-portrait-dpr2 | 0.87 | 1 ms | 28 slabs restored; latency paint p50 13 ms |
| webkit-ipad-landscape | 0.92 | 0 ms | |
| webkit-ipad-portrait | 0.92 | 0 ms | |
| webkit-phone-390 | 1.00 | 0 ms | |
| chromium-laptop-1440 | 0.99 | 0.1 ms | |

Full gate on integrate: biome on the whole repo, tsc for ink and web, vitest ink 66 and web 254, config_api pytest 21.

Noted for other owners:
- AppShell.tsx:171 has a sticky header at tablet width and up.
- QuestionPage, ReviewPage, ExamPage and ReaderPage have sticky bars.
- These may cost WebKit the same full-page repaint. I fixed none of them; they are not my files.
